views.title: Read the edge condition (reading step 3 of 6)
views.label: Recorded reading step 3 of 6 for the proper coloring statement
views.caption: Step 3 of 6 of Definograph’s Visual sequence, “Read the edge condition”: the assumption that u and v are adjacent in G, in its logical place.

views.title: Follow the coloring (reading step 4 of 6)
views.label: Recorded reading step 4 of 6 for the proper coloring statement
views.caption: Step 4 of 6 of Definograph’s Visual sequence, “Follow the coloring”. Its stage label, Construction, means that the step builds part of the conclusion: here c(u), one side of c(u) ≠ c(v). The figure shows the rule the coloring c carries for every edge; v₁ and v₂ stand for the two endpoints of any edge, not for u and v.

context.alt: Definograph in a browser, reading the statement What a proper coloring requires at step 4 of 6, Follow the coloring. context.caption: The Definograph window reading the menu statement “What a proper coloring requires”, at step 4 of 6 of its Visual sequence, captured at twice the display density. The Whole statement outline on the right shows where the step sits in the statement.

views.title: Read the membership condition (reading step 7 of 9)
views.label: Recorded reading step 7 of 9 for the ε-ball statement

views.title: Locate the source region (reading step 3 of 7)
views.label: Recorded reading step 3 of 7 for the partial equivalence statement
views.caption: Step 3 of 7 of the Visual sequence, “Locate the source region”: the two carriers, the designated regions e.source and e.target, and the maps between them. The figure draws both round trips because a PartialEquiv contains a law for each; the statement asserts only the one that starts in the source region.
